modules.title: Users
modules.summary: Central identity registry — accounts, roles, company-line access, and login credentials that every document and audit trail links back to.

sections.heading: What is this screen?
sections.content: The master registry of every system user — the login identity, role assignment, and company-line access behind every document, invoice, booking, and container movement created in the system. Every operational record stores a user_id, so this screen is the anchor for accountability and audit trails.

steps.title: Open Users
steps.desc: Sidebar → Administration → Users.

steps.title: Search & Locate
steps.desc: Filter by name, email, role, company, or active status.

steps.title: Enter Details & Save
steps.desc: Set credentials, role, company-line access, and active flag.

steps.title: System Validates
steps.desc: Checks unique email/login, role assignment, and company access.

steps.title: User Ready in System
outcomes: Can sign in with assigned role permissions
Linked to documents and audit trails

sections.heading: Fields stored
rows: Required and unique system-wide; 4-30 chars, letters/numbers/dot/underscore/dash only; used to log in
Required and unique system-wide; used for notifications and password resets
Required on create (min 6, confirmed); optional on edit — leaving it blank keeps the existing password
Optional unique integer; internal HR/staff ID
Dropdown of configured Roles; grants the account its permissions
Multi-select of company codes/branches the user may switch between
Default active company context for the account
Active / Inactive; inactive users cannot log in

sections.heading: Auto-inactive rule
sections.content: Saving a user with no Role selected automatically forces the account to Inactive (is_active = 0), preventing an unprivileged account from being left active.

sections.heading: Listing & search
sections.content: Paginated 30 per page, ordered alphabetically by username. Filters: Username, Full Name, Status, Role, Company Code, and Country.

sections.heading: Bulk actions
items: Bulk Assign Company Code — attach one or more company codes to every selected user at once.
Bulk Toggle Status — flip active/inactive for the selected users; an administrator cannot toggle their own status.
Reset Assigned Lines — refresh assigned company-line mappings for all users after new company branches are added.

sections.heading: Create & edit rules
items: Username, Email, and Employee Number (when provided) must each be unique system-wide; edit checks exclude the user being updated.
Password is required on create and optional on edit.
Assigned company codes resolve into the assigned_lines relation, which is what lets a user switch company context from their own Profile screen.

sections.heading: Profile & activity metrics
sections.content: Each user has a personal Profile screen showing account details plus live counters: total Quotations, Export BLs, Import Bookings, and Invoices created by that user. Users can update their own avatar and default company line there.

sections.heading: Delete rules
sections.content: Deleting a user permanently removes the account. Historical documents (quotations, BLs, invoices, activity logs) keep their stored user_id, but the deleted user disappears from staff dropdowns — prefer Inactive over Delete for departed staff when audit continuity matters.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.content: Users are the identity layer everything else hangs off. Role and Assigned Company misconfiguration is the most common reason staff can't see the branch data they need, and forgetting to deactivate departed employees is a real security exposure.

modules.title: Roles
modules.summary: Named permission bundles (job positions) attached to Users — the authorization backbone behind menus, buttons, and controller access checks.

sections.heading: What is this screen?
sections.content: Defines job-position Roles (e.g. Documentation Manager, Accountant, Sales Agent) and the exact system permissions bundled into each. Rather than granting permissions per user, a Role is attached to a User and every permission enabled on that Role is inherited automatically.

steps.title: Open Roles
steps.desc: Sidebar → Administration → Roles.

steps.title: Search & Locate
steps.desc: Find a job-position role by name or description.

steps.title: Set Permissions & Save
steps.desc: Bundle screen/action permissions for the role.

steps.title: System Applies Access
steps.desc: Users with this role inherit the permission set immediately.

steps.title: Role Controls Access
outcomes: Users inherit the bundled permissions
No need to grant permissions per user

sections.heading: Fields stored
rows: Auto-linked to the active company context at creation
Checklist of permission IDs grouped by module (Booking, Quotations, Invoices, Container Control, Vessel & Voyage, Master Data, etc.)

sections.heading: Listing & search
sections.content: Paginated 30 per page, ordered alphabetically by role name. Columns show the role name, a permission summary, and the users currently assigned to it.

sections.heading: Create & edit rules
items: Role Name is required and must be unique; the edit check excludes the role being edited.
Permissions can be checked individually or by whole module group.
Saving an edit re-syncs the full permission set and flushes the permission cache immediately, so active sessions pick up the change without needing to log out.

sections.heading: Viewing role details
sections.content: The Show page renders a read-only, module-grouped breakdown of a role's exact permissions, so an admin can audit what a role can do without risking an accidental edit.

sections.heading: How roles govern access
items: Sidebar menu items only render if the user's role holds the matching module-list permission.
Create/Edit/Delete/Export/Approve buttons on a screen check role permissions before they render.
Controllers re-check the same permissions server-side through authorization guards, independent of what the UI shows.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.content: Over-permissioning a role risks unauthorized financial actions or data changes; under-permissioning blocks routine work like issuing invoices or delivery orders. Because the permission cache is flushed on every save, role edits take effect immediately for users already logged in.

modules.title: Feature Flags
modules.summary: Per-user/company toggles that show or hide entire modules and sub-features without touching data or role permissions.

sections.heading: What is this screen?
sections.content: An admin control panel that turns whole sub-systems on or off — CRM, Custody, EDI, Trucking Guarantees, Storage/Detention calculations, QuickBooks accounts, and more. Disabling a flag hides the module from the UI (sidebar, buttons, routes) without deleting data or changing role permissions.

steps.title: Open Feature Flags
steps.desc: Sidebar → Administration → Feature Flags.

steps.title: Pick Scope
steps.desc: Choose Global or a specific user, then review flag groups.

steps.title: Save Configuration
steps.desc: Confirm which CRM, EDI, Custody, Trucking, or QB flags apply.

steps.title: System Rebuilds Menus
steps.desc: Sidebar and routes hide/show based on the saved flags.

steps.title: Modules Reflect Flags
outcomes: Disabled modules disappear from the UI
Enabled modules become reachable immediately

sections.heading: Fields stored
rows: The account the flag setting applies to; left unselected edits the company default/global scope
Internal string identifier, e.g. custody, demurrage, crm, edi

sections.heading: Flag groups
rows: ports_terminals, settings, agents_list, customers_list, suppliers_list, banks, exchange_rates, excel_templates
summary_booking, import_booking, export_booking, do_print_counter, bl_gates, manifest_xml, service_bl
invoice_gates, receipt_gates, credit_note, refund_gates, customer_statements, costs, qb_accounts

sections.heading: User selection & global scope
sections.content: A Super Admin dropdown lets an admin pick any non-super-admin user to view and edit that user's specific flags. Leaving no user selected edits the company's default/global flag state instead.

sections.heading: Save rules
items: Submitting the form only sends the flag keys that are currently checked.
Every checked key gets an updateOrCreate to enabled = true for the target scope.
Every key left unchecked is updated to enabled = false for that same scope.

sections.heading: How flags govern the app
items: Every check runs through the global featureFlagHelper('flag_key') helper.
Sidebar sections and sub-menu links only render when their flag evaluates true.
Screen-level controls (calculators, export buttons, whole action groups) check the same helper before rendering.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.content: Different agencies run different business models — one company may not use Custody or EDI at all. Feature Flags let each deployment be tailored without touching code, keeping unused modules out of operational staff's way.

modules.title: Journal
modules.summary: In-app release-notes / changelog bulletin with per-user read tracking, keeping staff informed of business-logic and workflow changes.

sections.heading: What is this screen?
sections.content: An internal changelog and release-notes bulletin. Admins publish entries categorized by module; every user can browse, search, and filter historical updates, and the system tracks per-user read/unread state so nothing important gets missed.

steps.title: Open Journal
steps.desc: Navbar/Sidebar → Journal (users) or Admin → Journals.

steps.title: Browse Updates
steps.desc: Search and filter release notes by module or date.

steps.title: Complete the Action
steps.desc: Users update read state; admins write categorized changelog entries.

steps.title: System Tracks State
steps.desc: Per-user read/unread is stored so important notes stay visible.

steps.title: Changelog Stays Current
outcomes: Users see what is still unread
Published notes are searchable historically

sections.heading: Fields stored
rows: Required classification (Booking, Quotations, Invoices, Containers, Voyages, EDI, Trucking, General, etc.)
published_at — drives sort order and the month filter
Per-user record in user_journal tracking who has read which entry

sections.heading: User view
sections.content: All users see header counters for Unread and Read entries, a free-text search over title/description, a Month filter, and a Module filter.

sections.heading: Read / unread controls
items: Clicking an unread card marks it read via AJAX and updates the navbar badge live.
A read entry can be flipped back to unread.
'Mark Visible Page as Read' marks the current page's 15 entries at once.
'Mark All as Read' / 'Mark All as Unread' apply to every historical entry for that user.

sections.heading: Admin publishing
items: Super Admins create/edit entries with Title, Module, Publication Date, and Description.
Deleting an entry also purges every per-user read-tracking row for it from user_journal.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.content: As calculation formulas, export formats, and validation rules evolve, the Journal reliably notifies operational staff inside the tool they already work in — closing the gap that a hallway announcement or a missed email would leave.

modules.title: System Logs
modules.summary: Super-admin-only exception/error monitoring dashboard that aggregates runtime failures across every module.

sections.heading: What is this screen?
sections.content: An exception-monitoring dashboard for Super Administrators. It captures runtime errors, unhandled exceptions, database failures, and EDI transmission errors from every module and presents them as a searchable, aggregated feed instead of raw server log files.

steps.title: Open System Logs
steps.desc: Sidebar → Administration → System Logs (Super Admin only).

steps.title: Filter Exceptions
steps.desc: Narrow by date, module, message, or EDI/runtime error type.

steps.title: Inspect Grouped Hits
steps.desc: Review aggregated exceptions and drill into a single occurrence.

steps.title: System Aggregates Errors
steps.desc: Repeated exceptions are grouped so patterns are easy to spot.

steps.title: Ops Can Act Fast
outcomes: Root causes are easier to isolate
Exports support incident follow-up

sections.heading: Fields stored
rows: JSON payload: file path, line number, exception class, stack trace
Named route executing when the failure occurred
Full request URL and HTTP method
Who and which company context triggered it

sections.heading: Grouped aggregation
sections.content: To avoid drowning in duplicate rows, the listing groups logs by (level + message + route_name) and shows an Occurrence Count plus First Seen / Last Seen timestamps instead of one row per hit.

sections.heading: Listing & filters
sections.content: Paginated 50 grouped entries per page, ordered by Last Seen descending. Header cards total Errors and Warnings for the selected period. Filters: date preset (Today / Last 7 Days / Last 30 Days) or a custom date range, Level, User (only users who triggered a logged error in range), and free-text search over message/URL/route.

sections.heading: Detail view & export
sections.content: Opening a grouped entry shows the latest occurrence with user/role/company context, full request details, and the complete, un-truncated stack trace. A Download action exports a plain-text diagnostic file (system-log-{id}.txt) formatted for developer or AI-assisted troubleshooting.

sections.heading: Clear logs
sections.content: Clearing logs deletes every record matching the currently applied filters. It is blocked entirely unless a date filter (preset or explicit range) is active, preventing an accidental full-table wipe.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.content: Failed invoice calculations, broken import routines, or EDI generation errors often fail silently in the background. This screen is how they surface — letting an admin trace the exact user, request, and payload involved before it causes a financial or operational problem.

modules.title: Activity Logs
modules.summary: System-wide data audit trail recording every create/update/delete on core business records with full before/after field diffs.

sections.heading: What is this screen?
sections.content: The application's central audit trail. Every time a user creates, edits, or deletes a tracked business object — Bookings, Quotations, Invoices, Container Control records, Customers, Master Data — an Activity Log entry is written automatically recording who did it, when, and a full field-by-field before/after comparison.

steps.title: Open Activity Logs
steps.desc: Sidebar → Administration → Activity Logs.

steps.title: Search the Audit Trail
steps.desc: Filter by user, model, action, or date range.

steps.title: Inspect the Change
steps.desc: Open the entry to see who changed what, and which fields moved.

steps.title: System Auto-Logs Events
steps.desc: Create/edit/delete of tracked objects writes an audit row automatically.

steps.title: Full Accountability
outcomes: Every tracked change has a user + timestamp
Field-level diffs support investigations

sections.heading: Fields stored
rows: Model category (Booking, Quotation, Container, Invoice, Customer, etc.)
Human-readable summary with reference numbers, e.g. 'updated Booking BK-202609-001'
Polymorphic link (subject_type + subject_id) to the exact record changed
The employee who performed the action
JSON of old values vs. new values

sections.heading: Listing & search
sections.content: Paginated 50 per page, newest first. Filters: Event type, Model Type, a reference-number search (BL, booking, container, invoice, or customer code), a free-text description search, and a start/end date range.

sections.heading: Field-by-field diffs
sections.content: Clicking a row opens an AJAX change-summary modal listing each changed field name with its Old Value and New Value side by side — e.g. spotting that a container's tare weight moved from 2,200 kg to 2,400 kg, and who did it and when.

sections.heading: Model-specific audit views
sections.content: Some screens expose their own scoped timeline on top of the central list — e.g. a Booking's action menu opens activity-logs.booking, a full chronological history of every change made to that one booking since creation.

sections.heading: Automatic logging mechanism
sections.content: Logging is automatic via the LogsActivity model trait: any model using it observes its own created/updated/deleted events and records only the fields that actually changed. No controller ever writes a log entry manually.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.content: Unauthorized or mistaken edits to BL descriptions, freight rates, release statuses, or invoice lines carry real legal and financial weight. Activity Logs make every change traceable to an exact user, timestamp, and field — the difference between an accountable correction and an unexplained discrepancy.

modules.title: Charge Codes
modules.summary: Company-specific catalogue of billable charge names used by invoices, debit documents, and quotation tariffs.

sections.heading: What is this screen?
sections.content: The master catalogue of every billable line item the company can place on an Invoice or Debit (Cost) document, such as Ocean Freight, THC, Storage, or Administration Fee. Documents reference a row from this list rather than accepting a free-typed charge name. The catalogue is scoped by company_id, so each company maintains its own list.

steps.title: Open Charge Codes
steps.desc: Sidebar → Master Data → Charge Codes (requires 'charges' flag).

steps.title: Search & Locate
steps.desc: Filter by Name, Tax Code, Type, or Category.

steps.title: Enter Details & Save
steps.desc: Fill Name, Tax Portal Code, Type, and optional QB Account.

steps.title: System Validates
steps.desc: Checks required fields, unique name, and usage locks.

steps.title: Ready in System
outcomes: Active for Invoices, Costs & Tariffs
Static seeded codes stay protected

sections.heading: Fields stored
rows: Required display name; unique within the company
Required free-text tax/e-invoicing code, stored in the code column
Invoice: THC / Admin / Cleaning; Debit: fixed Owner Account option
QuickBooks chart-of-accounts link, shown only when integration is enabled
Optional name override used in QuickBooks
System-only identity used by automatic calculations; not editable on the form

sections.heading: Static system charges
sections.content: Seeded charges such as ADFE, OFRI/OFRE, IS/ES, ID/ED, PI/PE, and WARR are looked up by static_code by invoicing and storage/detention calculations. They have is_deletable = false and must remain available even if their display labels differ.

sections.heading: Listing & search
sections.content: Paginated 30 per page and ordered by ID. Filters can be combined: Name, Tax Portal Code, Type (Debit / Invoice), and Category (THC / Admin / Cleaning). Each row shows a live count of invoices using that charge name.

sections.heading: Create & edit rules
items: Name and Tax Portal Code are required; Type defaults to Invoice and Category is optional.
Name must be an exact, case-sensitive unique value within the current company.
If a charge is already used by an Invoice or Quotation Tariff, its Name and Type cannot be changed.
Tax Portal Code, Category, and QuickBooks settings remain editable even when the charge is in use.

sections.heading: Delete rules
sections.content: Delete is shown only when the charge is used by zero invoices and is_deletable is true. Seeded static charges can never be deleted. Eligible deletes require confirmation.

sections.heading: Sync to companies
sections.content: A row action and bulk checkbox mode can copy charge setup to other companies in the same group, avoiding manual recreation in each sister company.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.content: Charge Codes defines the vocabulary used by invoices, costs, and quotation tariffs. Static-code rows are especially important because automated Administration Fee, Ocean Freight, Storage, Demurrage/Detention, Power, and War Risk logic depends on them.

modules.title: Port & Terminal
modules.summary: Global port and terminal/depot registry, including per-company terminal display-code mappings.

sections.heading: What is this screen?
sections.content: Ports and Terminals are global master data shared by every company. A Port is a country-linked top-level location; a Terminal or Depot is a facility within a port that is referenced by Movements, Bookings, and depot-specific Damage List rates.

sections.heading: Access
rows: Ports-List; Terminals-List additionally for Terminal Mappings

steps.title: Open Port & Terminal
steps.desc: Sidebar → Master Data → Port & Terminal (ports_terminals flag).

steps.title: Search Locations
steps.desc: Filter ports/terminals by code, name, or country.

steps.title: Enter Details & Save
steps.desc: Set code, name, country, and terminal-in-port relationships.

steps.title: System Protects Identity
steps.desc: Static Code stays locked; used ports/terminals cannot be removed.

steps.title: Ready for Operations
outcomes: Movements and bookings can reference the location
Terminal mappings feed depot-specific screens

sections.heading: Fields stored
rows: Name, globally unique Code, and Country
Code, Type (Terminal id 3 or Depot id 4), and immutable Static Code
old_code, per-company editable code, terminal_id, port_id, type_id, company_id

sections.heading: Listing & search
sections.content: The global Port list is paginated 30 per page and ordered by ID. Filters: Name, Code, and Country. The eye action opens all Terminal/Depot rows under a port.

sections.heading: Create & edit rules
items: The Port and all of its Terminal rows are maintained together in one repeatable-row form.
Port Code and Port Name must each be globally unique; edit checks exclude the current port.
A new terminal's static_code is copied from its original Code and never changes.
Later edits match a terminal by port_id + static_code, allowing its displayed Code to be renamed safely.
An existing terminal row cannot be removed from the edit form after it has Movement records.

sections.heading: Static Code identity
sections.content: static_code is the terminal's permanent identity anchor. Renaming the visible Code does not break Movement history, Damage entries, mappings, or other records because those continue to reference the same terminal_id.

sections.heading: Delete rules
sections.content: A Port cannot be deleted while it has related Voyage Port records. If clear, deleting the Port deletes all of its Terminal rows; this full-Port path does not perform the per-terminal Movement check used by the Edit form.

sections.heading: Terminal Mappings
items: Creating a Terminal automatically creates one mapping row per company.
old_code freezes the Terminal Code at creation; code starts with the same value and is editable per company.
Choose a Port to edit the current company's mapped codes; there is no manual Create or Delete action.
Deleting the underlying Terminal automatically removes its mappings.

sections.heading: Current mapping limitation
sections.content: The per-company mapped code is labeling infrastructure, but at the documented point it is not yet consumed by outbound export or EDI features.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.content: Voyages, Bookings, Movement Control, and depot-specific Damage rates all depend on this shared location hierarchy. Because it is global, incorrect data can affect every company.

modules.title: Agents List
modules.summary: Company-scoped registry of shipping agents/representatives linked to Principal Lines, referenced by Quotations.

sections.heading: What is this screen?
sections.content: The catalogue of shipping agents and representatives who act on behalf of the company's vessel lines/principals at various ports and countries — handling local port calls, documentation, and customs clearance. Each Agent links to one or more Principal Lines and is referenced by Quotations when issuing freight offers.

steps.title: Open Agents
steps.desc: Sidebar → Master Data → Agents (agents_list flag).

steps.title: Search Agents
steps.desc: Filter by name, country, or related principal/line.

steps.title: Enter Details & Save
steps.desc: Capture agent identity and representation details for the line.

steps.title: System Validates Record
steps.desc: Required fields and uniqueness rules are checked before save.

steps.title: Agent Available Downstream
outcomes: Voyages and documentation can pick the agent
Local handling parties stay consistent

sections.heading: Fields stored
rows: Required multi-select of Lines with type 9 or 2 under the current company; stored in the agent_principals pivot table
Active / Inactive; inactive agents are hidden from operational dropdowns

sections.heading: Listing & search
sections.content: Paginated 30 per page, ordered by ID. Filters — Name, Country, and Principal (line name) — are combinable. Columns show name, country, city, a bulleted list of linked Principal Lines, and an Active/Inactive badge.

sections.heading: Create & edit rules
items: Name, Country, Address, Phone, Email, and at least one Principal Line are required.
Name must be unique within the current company; the check excludes the record itself on edit — a duplicate submission shows 'Agent Name Already Exists'.
Selecting Principal Lines writes agent_principals pivot rows; on edit the existing links are deleted and re-inserted with the new selection.

sections.heading: Delete rules
sections.content: Before showing the delete confirmation, an AJAX check looks for any Quotation referencing the agent. If one exists, deletion is blocked with 'Sorry, you can't delete this agent. There are quotations related to it.' Only an agent with zero linked quotations can be deleted.

sections.heading: How this feeds other modules
sections.content: Quotations select an Agent to record which office is representing the freight quote. Vessel & Principal Lines use the agent_principals link to filter which agents are valid for a given line when building voyage itineraries and booking documents.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.content: Accurate agent contact details and Principal Line links keep quotations and freight documents reflecting the correct local representation, and the quotation-linked delete guard prevents breaking historical commercial offers.

modules.title: Suppliers List
modules.summary: Supplier profiles and their dated, criteria-based charge-item price lists used to build Cost invoices.

sections.heading: What is this screen?
sections.content: The company master registry of external suppliers—depots, truckers, terminal operators, sellers, lessors, haulage, and service providers. Each supplier also owns a repeatable Charge Items price list that supplies the selectable services and default prices for Cost (Debit) invoices.

steps.title: Open Suppliers
steps.desc: Sidebar → Master Data → Suppliers List (suppliers_list flag).

steps.title: Search Suppliers
steps.desc: Locate a depot, trucker, terminal, or service provider.

steps.title: Set Profile & Rates
steps.desc: Maintain supplier data and repeatable Charge Item price rows.

steps.title: System Links Cost Rates
steps.desc: Cost invoices look up supplier charge items for selectable rates.

steps.title: Supplier Ready for Costing
outcomes: Cost documents can pull negotiated rates
Export supports offline review

sections.heading: Supplier profile
rows: Currencies normally used by the supplier
Any combination of Depot, Services Provider, Seller, Trucker, Lessor, Haulage, Terminal

sections.heading: Charge Item fields
rows: Optional Terminal, Full/Empty status, Shipment Type, Equipment Type, and Cargo Type
Category, Sub Category, Code, Payer, and optional Equivalent Item
Valid From / Valid To date range

sections.heading: Create & edit rules
items: Required supplier fields: unique Name, Country, Address, Phone, and Email.
Charge Items are optional repeatable rows and each can have its own validity window.
A Charge Item already referenced by a Cost Description cannot be removed; attempting it rejects the entire supplier save.
An in-use Charge Item may remain in place while its other fields are edited.

sections.heading: Supplier view
sections.content: The read-only Show page opens in a new tab and provides a searchable, paginated price list. It can filter by Description, Equivalent Item, status/type fields, currency, category, amount, Invoice Type, Terminal, and validity dates.

sections.heading: How Cost invoices find rates
items: The selected Supplier Type limits the supplier dropdown to suppliers carrying that classification.
Supplier + Invoice Type + Operation Date selects only that supplier's Charge Items valid on the operation date.
Shipment Type, Container Status, and Equipment Type must match when specified; blank criteria generally match anything, while Transhipment matches only Transhipment.
Terminal rates determine the available Port list and can auto-select the port when all rates belong to one port.
Each Cost line references one validated supplier_charge_item_id and links direct containers, a BL Draft, or a Booking.
The stored Amount is a starting default; unit rate and quantity can be overridden per container on the invoice.

sections.heading: Cost totals
sections.content: Line total is quantity × unit rate, or the sum of per-container rate × quantity overrides. VAT Applied adds 14%. Invoice totals use the invoice's exchange rate and conversion direction without modifying the supplier Charge Item's stored reference amount.

sections.heading: Delete rules
sections.content: Deletion is blocked by active Cost invoices or any Cost Description referencing the supplier's Charge Items. Soft-deleted Cost records may be purged when no active costs remain; unused Charge Items are removed before the Supplier itself.

sections.heading: Export
sections.content: Excel export uses the active Supplier Name, Country, and Supplier Type filters. It outputs one row per Charge Item, repeating the supplier profile on each row to form a flat complete price list.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.content: Cost invoicing depends on this registry. Missing type classifications, mismatched criteria, or an expired Valid To date are common reasons an expected supplier rate does not appear.

modules.title: Banks
modules.summary: Company-owned bank-account master list used when recording receipt deposits.

sections.heading: What is this screen?
sections.content: The master list of the company's own bank accounts, used to record where a Receipt or Receipt Payment was deposited. It is not a registry of customer or supplier banks.

sections.heading: Access
rows: Suppliers permission group (Create / Edit / Show / Delete)

steps.title: Open Banks
steps.desc: Sidebar → Master Data → Banks (banks flag).

steps.title: Search Accounts
steps.desc: Filter company bank accounts by name, currency, or status.

steps.title: Enter Details & Save
steps.desc: Set account identity, currency, and active status.

steps.title: System Validates Account
steps.desc: Required fields and delete protection rules are enforced.

steps.title: Ready for Receipts
outcomes: Receipts can deposit to this company bank
Sync copies setup to sister companies

sections.heading: Fields stored
rows: Required fixed option: EGP / USD / EUR
Active / Inactive; new accounts start Active

sections.heading: Listing & search
sections.content: Company-scoped list, paginated 30 per page and ordered by Name then Currency. Filter by Bank Name or Currency. Add, Edit, and View all use modal dialogs on the list page.

sections.heading: Create & edit rules
items: Name, Currency, and Account Number are required.
Branch, IBAN, and SWIFT Code are optional.
There is no duplicate check for either bank name or account number.
Status is not part of Add/Edit; it is controlled from the list.

sections.heading: Active / inactive status
sections.content: The row badge toggles status after confirmation through an AJAX request. Inactive accounts remain attached to historical records but should not be offered for new Receipts.

sections.heading: Delete rules
sections.content: An account referenced by any Receipt or ReceiptPayment cannot be deleted. Its Delete action is hidden because can_delete is precomputed for the list. Use Inactive to retire an account while preserving history.

sections.heading: Sync to companies
sections.content: Individual and bulk Sync to Companies actions copy bank-account setup to other companies in the same group.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.content: Banks is the authoritative list for identifying which company account received money. Once used, an account is retained permanently for financial history.

modules.title: Exchange Rates
modules.summary: Global, non-overlapping currency-rate periods used for foreign-currency conversion to EGP.

sections.heading: What is this screen?
sections.content: Defines the conversion rate for each foreign Currency during an inclusive Date From / Date To period. Rates are global—there is no company_id—so every company shares the same periods. EGP is excluded because no EGP-to-EGP rate is needed.

steps.title: Open Exchange Rates
steps.desc: Sidebar → Master Data → Exchange Rates (exchange_rates flag).

steps.title: Find a Period
steps.desc: Locate currency rows by date-from / date-to window.

steps.title: Enter Rate & Dates
steps.desc: Set foreign currency, rate value, and inclusive date range (EGP excluded).

steps.title: System Shares Globally
steps.desc: Rates are global (no company_id) and apply across all companies.

steps.title: Conversion Ready
outcomes: Documents convert using the active period rate
Overlapping/invalid periods are blocked

sections.heading: Fields stored
rows: Numeric conversion rate to the base currency
Inclusive validity window, non-overlapping for the same currency

sections.heading: Listing & search
sections.content: Paginated 10 per page and ordered by newest Date From. Filter by Currency and date range; date filtering returns any period that overlaps the search range. A period covering today receives an Active badge.

sections.heading: Add rates
items: Add one or more Currency + Rate rows sharing a single Date From / Date To range.
The same currency cannot appear twice in the submitted batch.
Each row is checked for overlap with an existing period for that currency.
If any currency conflicts, the entire batch is rejected and the conflicting currencies are named.
When all checks pass, every row is inserted together in a database transaction.

sections.heading: Edit rates
sections.content: Edit changes one row's Currency, Rate, and dates. The same overlap validation applies while excluding the current row itself.

sections.heading: Delete behavior
sections.content: Deletion only requires confirmation and has no in-use guard. Previously generated output keeps its calculated value, but later recalculation for that historical date may fail or differ because rates are looked up live rather than stored by reference.

sections.heading: How rates are consumed
sections.content: Conversion code looks up the period covering the relevant date (or now), scoped to the currency and ordered by Date From descending. This supports QuickBooks conversion sync and shared PDF/report helpers.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.content: Foreign-currency conversion depends on continuous, non-overlapping coverage. A gap between periods means no rate can be found for calculations on those dates.

modules.title: Equipment Types
modules.summary: Master catalogue of container types/sizes (e.g. 20 DV, 40 HC) used across the whole system.

sections.heading: What is this screen?
sections.content: Defines the catalogue of container 'types/sizes' a company works with (e.g. 20 DV, 40 HC, 20 RF, 40 FR, 20 TK). This is master/reference data — it does not represent a physical box, it represents a category that many physical boxes belong to. Every physical container (Container List) must link to one of these types.

steps.title: Open Equipment Types
steps.desc: Sidebar → Container Control → Equipment Types.

steps.title: Search Types
steps.desc: Filter by code/size such as 20 DV, 40 HC, or 20 RF.

steps.title: Enter Type Details
steps.desc: Define type/size category used by physical containers and tariffs.

steps.title: System Applies Locks
steps.desc: Price Lock and usage rules protect types already referenced.

steps.title: Type Feeds Operations
outcomes: Container List and Radar group by this type
Tariffs and bookings reuse the catalogue

sections.heading: Feeds these modules
items: Container List — each container picks its type here
Movement Control — type is shown/validated on every movement & booking link
Bookings — a booking requests containers of a specific type/qty
Trucker Guarantee — deposit amounts are per equipment type

sections.heading: Fields stored
rows: Free text, e.g. '20 DV'. Leading number is auto-extracted and stored separately as Size.
Exactly one of: Dry / Special Equipment / Reefer
Reference monetary value, used by Trucker Guarantee deposit calc
Currency the Price is expressed in
Owning company (multi-tenant — each company sees only its own list)

sections.heading: Listing & search
sections.content: Paginated (30/page), ordered by creation order (ID). Filters: Size/Type (free text) and Category (dropdown). Both filters combine; clearing resets the list.

sections.heading: Create rules
items: Required: Size/Type (name) + Category. Everything else optional.
Duplicate check on (Name + Category) pair — same name with a DIFFERENT category is allowed.
Size is auto-extracted from leading digits: '20 DV' → 20, '40HC' → 40. No leading number → Size stays empty.
New record is auto-stamped with the creating user's company_id.

sections.heading: Edit rules
items: Same duplicate check as create (excludes the record being edited itself).
Size is re-extracted from the Name every time it's edited.

sections.heading: Price Lock rule
sections.content: If ANY physical container of this Equipment Type is currently held against an active Trucker Guarantee, the Price field becomes READ-ONLY on edit and any submitted value is ignored. It unlocks automatically once no container of that type is under an active guarantee.

sections.heading: Delete rules
sections.content: Cannot delete an Equipment Type that is still referenced by any container in the Container List. Only types with zero linked containers can be removed. Confirmation prompt is required before deleting.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.content: This must be configured before the rest of the system can be used meaningfully — you can't create a Container, validate a Movement, or price a Booking's container requirement without it. Keep size naming conventions consistent (e.g. always '20 DV') since several reports group by the extracted Size number.

modules.title: Container List
modules.summary: Master registry of every physical container (box) the agency works with — global, one row per container code.

sections.heading: What is this screen?
sections.content: The master registry of every PHYSICAL container in the system — one row per container number. Containers are GLOBAL master data: there is only ONE row per code in the whole system, never duplicated per company. If sister companies handle the same box, they share the exact same row. This is the anchor of the Container Control module.

steps.title: Open Container List
steps.desc: Sidebar → Container Control → Container List (containers flag).

steps.title: Search Containers
steps.desc: Filter by code, type, operator, stock badge, or depot.

steps.title: Enter / Upload Details
steps.desc: Set container number, type, operator; or import via template.

steps.title: System Derives Stock
steps.desc: Live stock badges come from movements; codes stay globally unique.

steps.title: Container in Fleet Registry
outcomes: In Stock / Out / Damaged badges update live
Import/export supports mass maintenance

sections.heading: Fields stored
rows: Container number, e.g. MSCU1234567 — unique across the ENTIRE system
Shipper-Owned vs Carrier-Owned — drives rules in Movement Control
The line currently operating this box; defaults to the creator's own line code if blank
Tare Weight / Max Payload / Production Year
Auto-calculated flag — NOT set manually once movement history exists

sections.heading: Default visibility rule
sections.content: By default the list only shows containers whose Operator Code matches the logged-in user's own line, is blank/unclaimed, or is an unrecognized code. This is bypassed when searching a specific container number, a specific Voyage, or filtering explicitly by Operator Code (multi-line companies) — a 'Cross' toggle widens a voyage search across sister companies too.

sections.heading: Search filters
items: Container Number (single or many, pasted)
Equipment Type / SOC-COC / Created By
In Stock — multi-select: Available / Not Available / Damaged / OFHR / WTOR
Vessel / Voyage (+ Shipment) / Leg
Operator Code — multi-select, multi-line ('MLH') companies only

sections.heading: Stock status badges (derived live)
rows: None of the above AND in_stock = 1
None of the above AND in_stock = 0

sections.heading: Create rules
items: Required: Equipment Type, Code, SOC/COC.
Code format: 4 letters + 7 digits + checksum (browser check); server only checks 4 letters + 7 digits + 11 chars. 'Force Insert' can override checksum-only failures.
Global uniqueness — code must not exist anywhere in the system.
Operator Code defaults to the creating user's own line code if left blank.
Certificate upload is stored under /certificat and linked after creation.

sections.heading: Edit rules & stock behaviour
items: Same code-format and uniqueness rules as create (excluding itself).
No movement history yet → In Stock is directly editable.
Has movement history → submitted In Stock value is IGNORED; it's recalculated from the latest movement instead ('Stock status determined by movements.').
Edit screen shows read-only info: movement count, latest movement (activity + date + recording company).

sections.heading: How 'In Stock' is calculated
items: No movement at all → In Stock = No
Latest movement is one of: On Hire, Receive From Consignee, Discharge Empty, Received Empty, Transfer Empty, Container Swapping, Gate In Empty, Received From Repair, Trangulation → In Stock = Yes
Any other latest activity → In Stock = No

sections.heading: Special case
sections.content: For agencies with line code OVP or OSL, an 'OFF Hire' movement ALSO counts as In Stock = Yes — this differs from the general rule where OFF Hire would not be a stock-in event.

sections.heading: Delete rules
sections.content: Cannot delete a container that has any related Movement, Booking, Container Repair, or Cost/BL invoice records. Only a container with zero history anywhere can be removed.

sections.heading: Bulk Import — Template / Upload / Overwrite
items: Template — static xlsx with expected columns (container_no, equipment_type, soc_coc, tare_weight, max_payload, production_year, container_ownership, operator_code, in_stock).

Import (Upload) — creates NEW containers only, keyed by container_no. Real ISO-6346 check-digit validation (skippable via Force Insert). Equipment Type must match exactly. Operator Code must exist in the active Operator Codes list. Failing rows are skipped and reported in a downloadable error report — passing rows still import.
Overwrite (auto-detect) — if the sheet only has container_no + operator_code, it's treated as a bulk Operator Code re-assignment (validated against active Operator Codes).
Overwrite (full mode) — matches rows by internal ID, requires SOC/COC, and only overwrites In Stock if the cell isn't empty.

sections.heading: Overwrite gap to know about
sections.content: Full Overwrite mode does NOT validate operator_code against the Operator Codes master list at all (unlike Import) — it's technically possible to bulk-write an operator code that doesn't exist. Prefer the 'Operator Code only' auto-detect mode or the Movement Control 'Assign Operator' tool for operator code changes.

sections.heading: Export
sections.content: Downloads containers.xlsx using the same filters currently applied on screen. Columns: id, container_no, equipment_type, soc_coc, tare_weight, max_payload, production_year, container_ownership, operator_code, in_stock, last_move. Multi-line ('MLH') companies get an extra 'line' column flagging when the latest mover differs from the operator_code on file.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.content: The single source of truth for 'what boxes do we have and what is their basic profile.' Stock Status is NOT typed in — it's a live reflection of Movement Control history. If Stock Status ever looks wrong, fix the Movement history, not the Container edit form.

modules.title: Equipment Status (Radar)
modules.summary: A read-only dashboard summarizing container counts per Equipment Type, split into status buckets.

sections.heading: What is this screen?
sections.content: A single summary dashboard answering: 'How many containers do we have, per Equipment Type, and what state is each group in right now?' It's read-only — every number is a live count of Container List rows grouped by Equipment Type. Clicking any number jumps straight into a pre-filtered Container List.

sections.heading: Access
rows: Containers-List (shared with Container List — no separate permission)

steps.title: Open Equipment Status
steps.desc: Sidebar → Container Control → Equipment Status (Radar).

steps.title: Scan Type Buckets
steps.desc: Review live counts per Equipment Type across stock states.

steps.title: Interpret Priority Buckets
steps.desc: Use the bucket priority order to understand the dominant state.

steps.title: System Counts Live
steps.desc: Read-only dashboard aggregates Container List rows with caching.

steps.title: Fleet Snapshot Ready
outcomes: Ops see stock health per type at a glance
No edit path — numbers always reflect live data

sections.heading: Table columns
rows: In stock and not flagged Damaged/Off-Hire/WTOR
Not in stock and not flagged Damaged/Off-Hire/WTOR
Sum of the 5 buckets, all statuses

sections.heading: Bucket priority order
items: Latest movement = SNTR → Damaged
Latest movement = OFHR → Off Hire
Latest movement = WTOR → WTOR
Otherwise split by in_stock flag: 1 = Available, 0 = Not Available

sections.heading: Scope: fleet-wide, not per-line
sections.content: Unlike Container List, Radar counts EVERY container in the system for every Equipment Type — it does NOT apply the 'only my own line' default visibility rule. It shows the whole physical fleet regardless of Operator Code.

sections.heading: Caching behaviour
sections.content: Results are cached for 5 minutes under 'container_radar_stats' (shared with the Dashboard widget). Cache clears immediately on container create/update/delete/import/overwrite — but NOT when a Movement record itself changes, so Radar can be up to 5 minutes stale right after a Gate-In or Sent-to-Repair movement. It self-corrects once the cache expires or a container record is next touched.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.content: The fastest way to answer 'what do we have, and is it usable?' without manually filtering the full Container List. Every cell doubles as a navigation shortcut into the correctly-filtered list.

modules.title: Operator Codes
modules.summary: Global master list of valid shipping-line codes used to validate the Operator Code field system-wide.

sections.heading: What is this screen?
sections.content: The master list of valid Operator Codes — short codes identifying which shipping line currently owns/operates a container. Unlike most master tables, this list is GLOBAL (no company_id) — one shared list for every company on the platform.

sections.heading: Access
rows: Containers (reuses the Containers permission group — no dedicated 'Operator Code' permission)

steps.desc: Sidebar → Container Control → Operator Codes.

steps.title: Search Codes
steps.desc: Locate a shipping-line operator code in the global list.

steps.desc: Add/update the short operator identity used on containers.

steps.title: System Soft-Protects
steps.desc: Delete is blocked when codes are in use; Refresh syncs shared list.

steps.title: Codes Validate Elsewhere
outcomes: Container operator fields accept only valid codes
One global list shared by every company

sections.heading: Validates these fields elsewhere
items: Container List — dropdown only offers ACTIVE codes; Import rejects unknown codes
Movement Control — Import rejects unknown codes; 'Assign Operator' bulk tool reads from here

sections.heading: Fields stored
rows: Short code (e.g. 'MSC') — always stored UPPERCASE + trimmed, unique system-wide
Optional label — the operator/line's full name
Only Active codes appear in dropdowns; inactive stay for history

sections.heading: List screen
sections.content: Paginated (30/page), alphabetical by Code. Shows Code, Name, Status badge, and a live CONTAINERS count of how many Container List rows currently use this exact code (quick 'in use' signal before editing/deleting).

sections.heading: Create / Edit rules
items: Code required, auto-uppercased + trimmed; Name optional.
Code must be unique system-wide (excluding itself on edit).
New codes are always Active by default — no toggle on the Add form.
Edit modal adds an 'Active' toggle — the only place is_active is changed.
Turning a code off does NOT touch existing Container/Movement records already using it.

sections.heading: Delete rule — soft protection
sections.content: Operator Code is stored as plain text (no foreign key), so deletion is checked manually: if ANY Container or Movement row uses this code, it is NOT deleted — instead it's automatically DEACTIVATED ('Operator Code is in use — deactivated instead of deleted.'). Only a code with zero usage anywhere is actually deleted.

sections.heading: 'Refresh' bulk sync
items: Scans every Company with a non-empty Line Code (excluding the internal 'YARD' company)
For each distinct Line Code: if it already exists here, it's skipped untouched
If it doesn't exist, a new Active Operator Code is created using the company's Line Name
Reports back: 'X new code(s) added, Y already existed.' — purely additive, never edits/deactivates/deletes

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.content: The gatekeeper for the Operator Code field across Containers and Movements. If a valid line code seems to be rejected everywhere, check here first: it either doesn't exist yet, or exists but is marked Inactive. Note: the Container 'Full Overwrite' import path bypasses this check entirely.

modules.title: Damage List
modules.summary: A price catalogue of standard damage types & repair rates — NOT a live log of currently-damaged containers.

sections.heading: Naming clarification — read first
sections.content: Despite the name, this screen is NOT a log of currently-damaged containers (that's the 'Damaged' badge on Container List / Equipment Status, driven by Movement Control's SNTR activity). This is a MASTER CATALOGUE / PRICE LIST of possible damage types and their standard repair cost — e.g. 'Dented panel — $45 per unit.' The Container Repair screen picks from this list.

steps.title: Open Damage List
steps.desc: Sidebar → Container Control → Damage List.

steps.title: Search Catalogue
steps.desc: Filter General or depot-specific damage price rows.

steps.title: Enter Price Details
steps.desc: Set damage description, depot scope, and chargeable amount.

steps.title: System Separates Concepts
steps.desc: This is a price catalogue — not the live Damaged stock badge.

steps.title: Repair Pricing Ready
outcomes: Repairs/quotations can pick priced damage items
Import keeps depot catalogues consistent

sections.heading: General vs Depot-specific damages
rows: depo_id = 'all' — applies everywhere, pinned at the top of page 1
depo_id = a Terminal ID (type = 4 / 'depot' terminals only)

sections.heading: Fields per damage type
rows: Required free text, e.g. 'Dented side panel'
Optional note on how it's normally fixed
Optional billing unit, e.g. 'per panel', 'flat rate'

sections.heading: List screen
sections.content: One row per depot (Terminal type 4) plus a pinned 'General Damages' row. An eye icon opens a searchable mini-table modal of that depot's damage types; a '+' icon opens the full add/edit page for that bucket.

sections.heading: Add/Edit rules (per depot or General)
items: One repeatable-row screen handles both add and edit for a bucket at once.
Damage Description required per row; Repair Type / Unit Type / Unit Rate optional.
Duplicate check within the same bucket: (Description + Unit Type + Unit Rate) must be unique, case-insensitive & trimmed.
Rows with an existing ID are updated in place; rows without an ID are inserted new.
Duplicates in a batch are skipped and reported — other valid rows in the same submit still save.

sections.heading: Delete rule
sections.content: Deletion is immediate — no confirmation guard, no 'in use' protection (unlike Operator Codes). This is safe because real Container Repair records store their own damage description text independently, so deleting a catalogue entry never retroactively changes a past repair.

sections.heading: Bulk Import — Template / Upload
items: Template columns: terminal, description, repair_type, unit_rate, unit_type.
Terminal blank / 'all' / 'general' / 'general damages' → saved as GENERAL. Any other value must match an existing Terminal CODE exactly.
Same duplicate rule as manual forms applies per row.
Every row is attempted — passing rows import immediately, failing rows are listed by row number in a combined result message.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.content: Think of it as the 'price book' for container damages — so anyone logging a real repair can pick from a standardised, pre-approved description and rate instead of re-typing free text every time. Get the General list right for damage that can happen anywhere; only add Depot-Specific entries where cost/description genuinely differs by location.

modules.title: Movement Control
modules.summary: Dated operational history per container — gate-in/out, load, discharge, on/off hire, repair — that drives stock, booking assignment, guarantees and draft BL dates.

sections.heading: What is this screen?
sections.content: Movement Control records the dated operational history of every container: gate-in/out, loading, discharge, on/off hire, repair and other configured activities. Each movement says what happened, when and where it happened, and which booking/vessel/voyage it belongs to. This is not just a tracking log — the latest movement controls the container's stock position and condition, valid next movements, booking-container assignment, trucker guarantee balance and, for a Load Full movement, the draft BL shipment date.

steps.title: Open Movement Control
steps.desc: Sidebar → Container Control → Movement Control (movement_control flag).

steps.title: Filter & Review Latest Move
steps.desc: Filter containers and review each box's latest non-deleted movement.

steps.title: Submit the Movement
steps.desc: Pick container, valid next activity, date, location, terminal and booking.

steps.title: System Validates Sequence
steps.desc: Checks next-activity rules, ETA/ETD window, and booking capacity.

steps.title: History Recorded & Propagated
outcomes: Stock, operator code and guarantee balances recalculate
Export All / Last / Summary Movement for reporting

sections.heading: Fields stored per movement
rows: The line/company that recorded the movement — matters when sister lines handle the same global container.
The physical container being moved. Required. Points to the one global Container List record for that code.
The global activity performed (e.g. ONHI, GIFU, LOFU, DCHF, SNTR, WTOR). Required. Choices come from the company's configured Next Possible Activities.
The company's own code for that activity, displayed beside the global movement code.
Event date and time. Required and cannot be in the future.
Full or Empty. Not chosen directly — copied from the company's Movement Activity Code configuration.
Port where the event occurred. Normally required.
Depot/terminal at the activity location. Normally required.
The linked booking. The database stores the booking record ID; the screen displays the booking reference number.
Vessel and voyage connected to the movement.
Displayed from the linked booking, not typed directly on the normal movement form.
Copied onto the movement from the container. ON HIRE restores the last operator that actually held the box and also updates Container List.
MLH companies can mark the movement as damaged. The displayed AV/DM flag is DM for SNTR, otherwise the Repair module's current flag wins, then this checkbox is the fallback.
Optional free text. Shown as a list column for the Sobek agency and included in exports.

sections.heading: What the list shows
sections.content: The main grid shows ONE row per container: its latest non-deleted movement, decided by full movement date/time and then movement ID when two records share the same time. It is ordered newest first and paginated 30 rows at a time. The row shows Container Number and Operator Code, Type/Size, global Movement Code, company Line Code, Movement Date, Full/Empty status, Booking, Vessel/Voyage, Activity Location, POL, POD, Terminal/Depot, Trucker and Created By. WTOR rows are greyed for easy recognition. Opening a row's details shows that container's FULL movement history, also newest first — editing and deleting individual history records happens from this history view, not directly in the main latest-row grid.

sections.heading: Search filters
items: Container Number (one or many, including pasted codes)
Type/Size
Activity Location
Terminal
Vessel/Voyage
Shipment: Import / Export (after selecting a voyage)
Movement Activity
Booking Number
From Date / To Date
Created By
Trucker
Operator Code (MLH companies)

sections.heading: Movement filter vs. "Last Movement" switch
sections.content: Without the switch, the movement filter helps find relevant records before the latest row per container is selected. With "Last Movement" enabled, the screen shows only containers whose CURRENT latest movement matches the selected activity — use it when the question is "Which containers are currently at WTOR?" rather than "Which containers have matching movement history?"

sections.heading: Default company scope & Cross-line
sections.content: The list normally shows movements recorded by the logged-in user's company. For MLH/sister-line operation, Cross widens results to companies sharing the same company-code group. Cross-line scope also activates when filtering by Operator Code, and a Booking Number search can widen to sister companies where company codes are enabled. A Container Number filter alone does NOT widen the movement-company scope — the row still belongs to whichever company recorded that movement.

sections.heading: Adding a single movement — normal flow
items: Select the container.
The screen loads valid next movement activities from that container's previous movement and the company's Movement Activity Codes setup.
Select the activity and movement date.
Select Activity Location and Terminal.
Select Booking, Vessel and Voyage when the activity requires shipment references.
Add optional Remarks / damaged condition and save.

sections.heading: Single movement rules
items: Required by default: Container, Movement Type, Movement Date, Activity Location, Terminal, Booking, Vessel and Voyage.
Booking, Vessel and Voyage are optional for: Receive Empty, Transfer Full, Receive Full, On Hire, Off Hire, Transfer Empty, Load Empty and Discharge Empty.
The movement date cannot be later than today.

Manually creating Load Full or Discharge Full requires the date to fall between the selected voyage-port ETA and ETD; no matching schedule rejects with "No ETA and ETD found for the selected voyage and port."
Editing recalculates Full/Empty status from the selected activity. If an assigning activity, container or booking changes, the old booking assignment is reversed and the new valid assignment is made.

sections.heading: Known inconsistency — ETA/ETD check on Edit
sections.content: The ETA/ETD date-window check runs on CREATE but is currently disabled on the EDIT path. Editing can therefore save a load/discharge date that the create form would reject.

sections.heading: Movement-sequence rules
items: Single movement: after the container is selected, the form offers its valid next activities — the server save mainly relies on that controlled dropdown.
Bulk movements: every selected row is checked against the container's previous and next history. If any row is invalid, the whole batch is rejected and no movement is created.
Excel import/overwrite: the activity is checked against the movement immediately before AND immediately after it, preventing a dated event from breaking either side of history.
The same activity twice in a row is normally rejected — import raises "Invalid movement sequence ... Expected: <allowed codes>".
If an activity has no per-company configuration/next-move rule, the system can behave as unrestricted in some paths — correct Movement Activity Code setup is essential before entering movements.

sections.heading: Cross-company Load → Discharge exception
sections.content: A cross-company exception allows a physical Load → Discharge handoff between sister companies even when that transition is not configured in the previous company's normal sequence. The bypass does NOT apply to a same-company Load → Discharge.

sections.heading: Bulk Movements — Voyage mode
items: Shipment Type → Vessel/Voyage → Movement Date → Load Containers
Select rows
Choose each valid Next Movement
Submit

sections.heading: Bulk Movements — Containers mode (MLH)
items: Paste Container Numbers → Choose Port/Terminal and Movement Date
Load Containers
Choose valid Next Movements
Submit

sections.heading: Bulk movement rules
items: Voyage mode loads containers from confirmed bookings on the selected voyage; imports add the correct discharge choice, exports add the appropriate gate-out or transhipment-load choice.
Containers already ending in a load move can be disabled, and a draft BL can block further load movements after gate-in.
Containers mode (MLH): unknown container codes are reported; containers with no movement history, or whose latest movement ends a cycle that must be handled via Voyage mode, are not accepted.

Bulk validation is ALL-OR-NOTHING — the service validates every selected row (date, references, sequence, booking capacity/type, duplicate movement rules) first. If one or more rows fail, zero rows are created. Only a fully valid batch is saved in one transaction.
For multi-port voyages, Port/Terminal may need to be selected per row. One Remarks value can be applied to the whole batch.

sections.heading: Excel template & Import
items: Template columns: container_no, movement_type, date, port_location, terminal, booking_no, vessel, voyage_no, remarkes, operator_code.
Upload accepts one worksheet only, up to 50 MB.
Container Number must already exist globally; Movement Type must match a global Movement Activity code; Port and Terminal must match existing codes.
Booking is matched by reference across the sister-company group; Vessel/Voyage is matched within the relevant company/sister group.
A supplied Operator Code must already exist in Operator Codes.
The movement is recorded under the booking's company when a sibling company booking is found; otherwise it uses the uploading company.

sections.heading: Import date & reference rules
items: The date accepts supported Excel/date formats but cannot be in the future.
Booking/Vessel/Voyage can be inherited from the booking or previous movement for valid mid-cycle activities; new-cycle activities do not inherit old booking/voyage data.
Mid-cycle movements must stay on the previous movement's booking, except where a summary booking relaxes that continuity rule.

Some reference-only activities allow Terminal to be blank. ON HIRE, OFF HIRE and Receive From Consignee have a broader import relaxation for Port/Terminal and shipment references — the relaxed set is not identical to every other entry path, so the template should not be used to bypass proper operational data.

sections.heading: Import is partial-success, not all-or-nothing
sections.content: Each row has its own transaction: valid rows are saved immediately, while invalid rows are skipped and collected into an error report. At the end, stock is recalculated for every affected container and the user sees the success count plus a download link for errors. When unresolved import errors exist, the list replaces the Import/Overwrite actions with "Show Errors" until those errors are handled.

sections.heading: Overwrite behaviour
items: Overwrite updates existing movements and matches each row by movement ID, not Container Number.
It only accepts movement IDs belonging to the uploader's sister-company group.
If the movement code is changed, the new code is validated against both the previous and next movement.
Successful rows update immediately; failed rows are reported — an overwrite can also finish with partial success.
Overwrite refreshes the linked booking-container terminal where that assignment already exists, then recalculates container stock.

sections.heading: Booking assignment & part-load rules
items: Assignment applies to: COC gate-out on an export booking, SOC Gate In Full / Receive From Shipper / Gate In Empty, Stuffing Full, and RXPF on an export booking.

For a regular export booking, the system must find an unassigned booking slot of the SAME equipment type; quantity, weight and package values are split from that slot onto the assigned container. No matching free slot rejects the movement instead of creating an invalid booking link.
Import and summary bookings can create the booking-container link without the same free-slot requirement.
Receive Empty releases the booking-container assignment. Deleting or changing an assigning movement reverses its old assignment so the booking quantity is available again.

Part-load bookings let one physical movement represent related parent/child bookings — import can reuse/collapse matching gate-out rows and collect child booking references in Remarks; matching Discharge Full rows are collapsed too rather than creating duplicate physical events.

sections.heading: Bulk vs. single/import assignment gap
sections.content: Single entry/import and Bulk Movements do not assign exactly the same set of activity types. Bulk currently auto-assigns export SNTS and STFU paths, while the single/import logic also covers COC GOMT, SOC gate-ins and RXPF. If booking assignment is the goal, confirm the Booking container details after a bulk move.

sections.heading: Automatic effects on other modules
rows: After create, edit, delete, bulk entry, import or overwrite, the container's latest non-deleted movement recalculates Container List In Stock. Stock-in activities set Available; other activities normally set Not Available. For OVP and OSL line codes, OFF Hire is a special stock-in event.
Each movement normally copies the Container List operator code. ON HIRE uses the operator from the latest prior movement when available, then writes that restored code back to Container List.
Creating Load Full (LOFU/LODF) recalculates the linked draft BL's shipment date from the latest Load Full date for its containers.

Movement create, update and delete trigger a guarantee-balance recalculation. Events such as WTOR/Gate Out can place a hold; Gate In, Stripping or Receive Empty can release it. SOC containers do not hold a trucker guarantee.
Recording a qualifying gate-out removes the earlier WTOR movement for the same container/booking where applicable, since the box is no longer waiting to be released.

sections.heading: Deleting movements
items: Deleting a movement is a soft delete — it disappears from normal history without physically erasing the database row.
Container stock is recalculated from the remaining latest movement and booking assignment effects are reversed where applicable.
A movement that assigned a container to a booking cannot be deleted when that booking already has a draft BL — the user is warned the movement cannot be deleted because the booking has a BL.
Bulk delete can partially succeed: protected rows are skipped while allowed rows are deleted, and the result reports both counts.
Repair workflow movements (SNTR / RCVR) and WTOR are protected in the history UI — they cannot be selected, edited or deleted there; they must be corrected through the workflow that created them.

sections.heading: Exports
rows: Exports all matching movement rows, newest first, using the current search/cross-line scope. Includes Container/Type, SOC/COC, global and line movement codes, F/E, event date, port/depot, AV/DM, agency, booking, trucker, vessel/voyage, Remarks, POL and POD.
Exports only the newest matching row per container, using movement date and ID as the tie-breaker.
Uses the current filters and can optionally request the container's last cycle.

sections.heading: Export naming note
sections.content: Despite the internal route/class names, the visible menu behavior is as described above: "All Movement" exports all matching history, while "Last Movement" exports one latest row per container. The separate MovementsExportAll implementation is a legacy/unwired exporter and is not the source of the current menu's Last Movement output.

sections.heading: Company-specific behaviour
rows: Shows Cross/Operator Code filters, Container Condition and the pasted-container Bulk Mode. Cross works within the sister-company code group, not across unrelated companies.
RCVC has special reference inheritance/relaxed handling in import and bulk processing.
OFF Hire counts as In Stock.
Remarks are displayed directly in the main movement grid.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.content: Movement Control is the operational source of truth for where each container is, what happened to it and what may happen next. A wrong date, booking or activity can change stock availability, block the next move, misassign booking capacity, alter guarantee balances or set the wrong draft BL shipment date. When a container status looks wrong, inspect its full chronological history first — correct the movement sequence rather than manually changing In Stock on the Container List.
